paragraphs.notes: Continuation page: the list runs on from the bottom of the previous page (p90) and no claim number, sub-paragraph letter or symbol label is printed anywhere on this page, so the marker above is descriptive and not printed text. The whole page body is one uninterrupted comma-separated enumeration of substituent group names that ends with a semicolon on the last line; it is recorded as a single paragraph. Printed line breaks are preserved as newlines rather than rejoined, because this text hyphenates group names mid-line as a matter of style (for example 'Cycloalkyl-alkinyloxycarbonylamino' on line 1), so a hyphen at the end of a line cannot be told apart from a hyphen belonging to the name, and rejoining would resolve that ambiguity by guessing. The affected line ends are line 14 ('Arylalkoxycarbonyl-'), line 15 ('Heteroaryl-') and line 18. Superscripts and subscripts are transcribed inline: R8, R9, R10 and R11 are printed as R with a superscript numeral, and the n and m in (CH2)n and (CH2)m are printed as subscripts. Several names are printed with the letter l missing from the alkinyl stem: 'Arylalkinyoxycarbonylamino' (line 5), 'Heteroarylalkinyoxycarbonylamino' (line 7), 'Heterocyclylalkinyoxycarbonylamino' (lines 9 and 18) and 'Arylalkinyoxy-carbonylamino' (line 15). These are reproduced as printed and not corrected; the English keeps the same defect visible as 'alkyny' rather than 'alkynyl'. Note that line 17 prints the full 'Heteroarylalkinyloxycarbonylamino'. Spacing oddities on line 32 are as printed: a double space before the third item and a space in '(CH2)n- Aryl'. A small ink speck sits above the word 'carbonylamino' on line 4; it is a scan artifact and carries no text.
